syllabus_topics: Introduction - constituent elements; access networks, physical media and information digitalization; core networks, switching and Internet structure; Degradation factors and performance metrics; layered organization and TCPI/IP architecture; historical evolution

Application layer – network applications, client-server and peer-to-peer architectures; notion of API and socket programming; Web and HTTP; E-mail; name management and DNS; file distribution; streaming; network management and SNMP
Transport layer: connectionless transport and UDP; reliability and TCP; congestion control and TCP

Network layer – data and control; IPv4 and IPv6 (addressing, fragmentation, configuration, resolution and address translation); routing algorithms, intra-AS routing and OSPF; inter-AS routing and BGP; ICMP; SDN
Link layer: error detection and correction; multiple access; local networks; layer 2 switching and addressing; virtualization and data center networks
assessment_rules: The final grade is 50% theoretical component grade + 50% laboratory component grade. The theoretical component grade is the minimum of the Oral defense of grade and the Exam. Students whose difference between theoretical and laboratory performance is greater than 3 points may be selected for a final oral defense, which replaces the theoretical component grade to rule out fraud. A minimum grade of 8/20 is required for the theoretical component and 9.5/20 for the laboratory component. The laboratory component grade is the average of the classifications of the 5 laboratory assignments.
bibliography: J. Kurose and K. Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach, 7th edition., Pearson (main)
institution: Universidade De Lisboa — LERC Eng. de Telecomunicações e Informática (IST)
degree: Licenciatura em Engenharia de Telecomunicações e Informática (LERC)
